predecessors.name: Spanish Empire
predecessors.text: central Chile from Copiapó to the Bío-Bío

ledger.x: 18 September 1810: Chile forms its First National Junta.
1813: the viceroy of Peru sends an army against Chile.
1-2 October 1814: the Disaster of Rancagua ends the Patria Vieja.
5 April 1818: Maipú, and the royalists fall back on Concepción.
1826: Chiloé, the last Spanish territory in Chile.
1843: Chile founds Fuerte Bulnes on the Strait of Magellan.
December 1861 - May 1862: the Occupation of Araucanía begins at Mulchén.
1862: Angol. Saavedra 'advanced with a group of 800 soldiers into the remnants of the town of Angol'; the page gives no founding date.
1866: a coastal fort between Lebu and the Imperial River.
7 June 1880: Chile holds Tacna and Arica.
January 1881: Lima is taken after Chorrillos and Miraflores.
23 July 1881: the Boundary Treaty with Argentina.

1881: Aisén. The treaty runs the line 'over the highest summits of the said Cordilleras which divide the waters'; Cliopatria's 1885 shape holds Aisén at 95 percent but no page opened names it, so the year is the treaty's, not a Chilean act there.
20 October 1883: the Treaty of Ancón ends the occupation of Tarapacá by cession.
29 October 1883: the Chilean occupation of Lima ends.
4 August 1884: the Chilean Expeditionary Forces embark at Callao.
9 September 1888: Chile takes possession of Easter Island.
20 October 1904: the occupation of the Bolivian coast ends in annexation.

wars.name: Chilean War of Independence
wars.outcome: The patriots lost at Rancagua (1-2 October 1814), won at Chacabuco (12 February 1817) and Maipú (5 April 1818), proclaimed independence on 12 February 1818, took Valdivia in 1820 and Chiloé in 1826.

wars.name: War of the Pacific
wars.outcome: Chile seized Antofagasta on 14 February 1879, took Tarapacá, Tacna, Arica and Lima, and gained Tarapacá by the Treaty of Ancón (20 October 1883); Bolivia signed a truce at Valparaíso on 4 April 1884 and ceded its coast in 1904.

wars.name: Occupation of Araucanía
wars.outcome: Chile advanced from the Bío-Bío and Malleco line (Mulchén 1861-62, Angol 1862, a coastal fort in 1866), founded Victoria (28 March 1881), put down the Mapuche rising of 5 November 1881 and re-founded Villarrica (1 January 1883); on 1 June 1883 'the whole…

wars.name: Tacna-Arica dispute
wars.outcome: Chile administered Tacna and Arica from 1880/1883; a plebiscite meant for 1893 never took place; Tarata returned to Peru on 1 September 1925; the Treaty of Lima (3 June 1929, effective 28 August) awarded Tacna to Peru and left Arica to Chile.

wars.name: Patagonian boundary dispute with Argentina
wars.outcome: The Boundary Treaty of 23 July 1881 divided Tierra del Fuego at 68°34' W and neutralised the Strait; 'In 1902, war was again avoided when King Edward VII of Britain agreed to mediate'; the Puna de Atacama was settled in 1899.

certainty.note: Unsurveyed frontiers: the Mapuche Araucanía until 1883, the Atacama desert and the Andes; the 1822 northern limit is not on any page.

The treaty line with Argentina (23 July 1881) runs 'over the highest summits of the said Cordilleras which divide the waters' and was fixed in the field only by the 1902 arbitration; the Bolivian coast and Tacna-Arica were occupied, not…
The 1904 treaty delimits the Bolivian boundary through 96 points; the 1929 Treaty of Lima fixes Peru's; the 1902 award and the 1881 treaty fix Argentina's.
